B1_event_loss.description: Controlled-rate file-open generation (rate-gen) against a policy-bound pod, comparing the generator's own attempted count against RuntimePlacementEvidence.Behavior counters and the node-wide DropCount.
B1_event_loss.runs_per_rate_note: Protocol's example progression (100/1k/5k/10k events/s) does not specify a repetition count for B1; n=1 run per rate is a documented, honest scope decision under real time constraints (this campaign is running many experiments serially against one live billed cluster), not concealed as a larger n. The rate sweep itself, not repetition count, is the primary independent variable being characterized.
B1_event_loss.methodology_note: Two harness bugs were found and fixed before this data is trustworthy -- see exclusions.md for the full account and discarded-runs/ for the invalidated attempts. (1) A capture race: without a linger period after the tool exits, the agent's revoke+forgetAll cycle could wipe per-cgroup counters before the next evidence tick captured them, producing spurious 100% loss. (2) A closure-gap confound: the generator started running at container start, racing ahead of the harness's own decision-minting + EnforcementReady wait, so measured loss partly reflected Task 04's admission-to-release gap, not eBPF observation capacity. Fixed via GATE_START (generation waits for a start signal touched only after EnforcementReady is confirmed) and a fixed post-generation wait spanning at least one full evidence tick before a single read (not "poll until first non-empty", which can catch a partial mid-tick snapshot).

B2_alternate_path_coverage.description: For each (probed syscall, target) pair, invoke a raw-syscall probe inside a policy-bound pod and compare RuntimePlacementEvidence.Behavior deltas against a wrapper-only baseline (an unrecognized probe mode that performs zero file/exec syscalls before exiting).
B2_alternate_path_coverage.methodology_note: Raw (non-delta) counters were found to include real, non-negligible wrapper overhead (the GATE_START wait loop and the shell's own fork+exec of the probe binary), confirmed by execDenied=2 appearing even for the openat2 case, which makes zero exec calls. A one-time wrapper-only baseline run (probe mode set to an unrecognized string, which altpath-probe's default case handles by exiting without any file/exec syscall) is subtracted from each case's counters; only the delta is attributed to the probed syscall. The altpath-execveat implementation additionally performs one precursor open() (needed for its dirfd+AT_EMPTY_PATH calling convention), so its fileOpenDenied delta is not itself evidence execveat was observed -- only execDenied is; a more direct execveat(AT_FDCWD, pathname, ...) invocation without a precursor open was not tested, and would very likely be an even more complete bypass.

B3_monitor_liveness.description: Creates a policy-bound long-running workload, captures a baseline evidence lastHeartbeat, kills the node's agent pod, and verifies (a) while genuinely dead, verify-evidence's monitor-heartbeat-fresh check correctly flags stale evidence, and (b) once recovered, it correctly does not.
B3_monitor_liveness.max_age_note: Set to 1.5x the 30s production evidence-tick interval. Two prior attempts used shorter or unmargined values and produced misleading results documented in exclusions.md: a max-age of 20s (less than one tick interval) flagged a genuinely healthy, freshly-ticked monitor as stale purely from normal tick-phase timing (a live monitor's heartbeat naturally ranges 0-30s old between ticks).
B3_monitor_liveness.recreation_block_mechanism: Temporary nodeSelector patch on the DaemonSet (a key no node satisfies), reverted via JSON-patch remove after the dead-monitor check. Node taints do NOT work here: the DaemonSet's pod template tolerates all taints ({"operator":"Exists"}).

B4_formal_synthesis.description: Not a script -- a synthesis of B1/B2/B3 findings against the required security property CompleteObs_Omega(I) <=> Coverage_Omega(I) AND NoLoss(I) AND MonitorLive(I), documented in summary.md.

sample_size_discipline: n = number of independent pod/run lifecycles, never assertions x runs.
